title: Daulat Khan Flees to Guru Nanak after the Slaying of His Sons

blocks.text: After the murder of Rai Bhoi and the spreading fear at court, confidence in Bairam Khan collapses and officials begin to scatter, hide, or think only of escape. The courtly world that had once rewarded Daulat Khan's house now feels exposed to arbitrary destruction.

News reaches Daulat Khan that his sons have been killed, and Daulat Khan fled toward Eminabad in search of the one refuge still imagined as trustworthy. The movement is both geographic and spiritual, carrying him away from compromised political power and toward Guru Nanak's presence.

By the end of the page he is no longer a grand court figure but a bereaved father hurrying to fall at the Guru's feet. That shift from office to supplication gives the next scene its emotional weight and moral urgency.
